e2/e2.phenotype: APOE ε2/ε2 Homozygote: Protective against Alzheimer's disease, but strongly associated with genetic predisposition to Type III Hyperlipoproteinemia (familial dysbetalipoproteinemia; requires secondary metabolic triggers).

caveats: Risk estimates are from predominantly European-ancestry cohorts and may not apply equally to other ancestries.
e2/e3.phenotype: APOE ε2/ε3 Heterozygous Carrier: One protective ε2 allele and one neutral ε3 allele (~10–15% population prevalence). Associated with ~40–50% lower relative risk (versus ε3/ε3) of Alzheimer's disease (absolute lifetime risk ~5–8% is a separate figure) and lower circulating LDL-cholesterol.

caveats: Risk estimates are from predominantly European-ancestry cohorts and may not apply equally to other ancestries.
e2/e4.phenotype: APOE ε2/ε4 Double Heterozygote: Carries one protective ε2 allele and one risk-elevating ε4 allele (~2% population prevalence). Overall Alzheimer's risk is intermediate between ε3/ε3 and ε3/ε4 (relative risk ~1.5–2× versus ε3/ε3; absolute lifetime risk ~15–20% is a separate figure).

caveats: Risk estimates are from predominantly European-ancestry cohorts and may not apply equally to other ancestries.
e3/e3.phenotype: APOE ε3/ε3 pattern: no ε2 or ε4 allele detected at rs429358 or rs7412 (the 2 APOE variants tested). This is the most common APOE genotype (~60–65% population frequency) and corresponds to the population-baseline lifetime risk for late-onset Alzheimer's disease, which is not an absence of risk.
e3/e3.significance: No ε2 or ε4 allele detected

caveats: Risk estimates are from predominantly European-ancestry cohorts and may not apply equally to other ancestries.
e3/e4.phenotype: APOE ε3/ε4 Heterozygous Carrier: One ε4 copy conferring a ~3–4× relative risk (versus ε3/ε3) of late-onset Alzheimer's disease (~20–25% population prevalence); the absolute lifetime risk ~25–35% is a separate figure. Cardiovascular health, regular aerobic exercise, ApoB management, and quality sleep are effective protective lifestyle modulators.

caveats: Risk estimates are from predominantly European-ancestry cohorts and may not apply equally to other ancestries.
e4/e4.phenotype: APOE ε4/ε4 Homozygote: Two copies of the ε4 allele (~2% population prevalence). Confers a ~12–15× relative risk (versus ε3/ε3) of late-onset Alzheimer's disease, and increased LDL/atherosclerosis susceptibility.

0.phenotype: No DPYD *2A (c.1905+1G>A) allele detected at this position. Other DPYD variants are not tested here, so DPD activity cannot be inferred.

1.drug_response: 5-Fluorouracil / Capecitabine: CPIC recommends reducing the starting dose by ≥50%
1.phenotype: One DPYD*2A (rs3918290) allele detected. This variant is associated with a high risk of life-threatening neutropenia and mucositis on fluoropyrimidines, and CPIC recommends a ≥50% dose reduction for carriers of one non-functional allele. DPD activity also depends on other DPYD variants that this array does not test, so a DPD activity status cannot be inferred from this one variant.

2.drug_response: 5-Fluorouracil / Capecitabine: CPIC recommends avoiding standard dosing (alternative therapy)
2.phenotype: Two DPYD*2A (rs3918290) alleles detected. Two copies of this variant are associated with severe, potentially fatal toxicity with standard 5-FU/capecitabine dosing, and CPIC recommends an alternative therapy. DPD activity also depends on other DPYD variants that this array does not test, so a DPD activity status cannot be inferred from this one variant.

rs3918290.limitation: Single-variant test: this assay covers only DPYD c.1905+1G>A (*2A), one of several CPIC-relevant DPYD variants. Not detecting it does not rule out reduced DPD activity from other variants.
rs3918290.tier_citation: CPIC guideline for DPYD and fluoropyrimidines, 2017 update
rs3918290.tier_rationale: CPIC lists this gene-drug pair at level A.

0.phenotype: No CYP2C19 *2 allele detected at this position. Other CYP2C19 alleles (for example *3, *17) are not tested here, so a metabolizer phenotype cannot be inferred.

1.phenotype: One CYP2C19*2 (rs4244285) allele detected. This variant is associated with reduced clopidogrel activation, and CPIC recommends an alternative agent for acute coronary syndrome in people with reduced CYP2C19 function. A metabolizer status needs CYP2C19 star-allele diplotyping, which this single-variant test does not do.

2.drug_response: Clopidogrel: Impaired activation (two *2 alleles; alternative drug recommended)
2.phenotype: Two CYP2C19*2 (rs4244285) alleles detected. Two copies of this variant are associated with significantly impaired clopidogrel activation, and CPIC indicates an alternative antiplatelet (ticagrelor/prasugrel). A metabolizer status needs CYP2C19 star-allele diplotyping, which this single-variant test does not do.

rs4244285.limitation: Incomplete star-allele coverage refusal: Interrogating an isolated SNP (e.g. *2) cannot rule out other active, decreased, or gain-of-function alleles (e.g. *3, *4, *17) not present on this array. A full metabolizer phenotype cannot and will not be inferred without complete haplotype sequencing.
rs4244285.tier_citation: CPIC guideline for CYP2C19 and clopidogrel, 2022 update
rs4244285.tier_rationale: CPIC lists this gene-drug pair at level A.

manifest.guardrail: ABSENCE OF A FINDING DOES NOT IMPLY ABSENCE OF GENETIC RISK. Lucidase analyzes only targeted single-nucleotide polymorphisms interrogated by consumer arrays. It does not perform full gene sequencing, does not analyze unprobed exonic or intronic regions, and cannot detect large copy-number variations (CNVs), balanced translocations, or structural repeats.
